title: Degree-zero compact-support vanishing for an ordinary middle extension
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum of [def-wf-middle-extension]: $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$, and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$ with chosen coefficient field $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Let $C_0$ be a smooth geometrically connected affine curve over $k_0$, meaning a separated finite-type affine $k_0$-scheme whose structure morphism is smooth of relative dimension one [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and whose base change to every field extension of $k_0$ is connected. Let $j_0:U_0\hookrightarrow C_0$ be a dense open immersion and let $\mathcal F_0$ be a lisse $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-Weil sheaf on $U_0$ in the finite-extension adic convention of [def-wf-middle-extension], with Weil structure as in [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Put $C=C_0\times_{k_0}k$ and write $j:U\hookrightarrow C$ and $\mathcal F$ for the geometric base changes. Write $j_*\mathcal F$ for the ordinary sheaf direct image of [def-wf-middle-extension], placed in degree zero, rather than the full complex $Rj_*\mathcal F$; it is a constructible sheaf on $C$ by [lem-a1-adic-middle-extension-constructible], so its compact-support cohomology is defined. In the completed integral, rationalized, common-finite-stage compact-support convention of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], after forgetting the Weil structure, one has
$$H_c^0(C,j_*\mathcal F)=0.$$
No purity, weight, or ramification condition on $\mathcal F_0$ is required.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph, degree-zero lissity argument; support interpretation in literature/milne-lectures-on-etale-cohomology_LEC.pdf, Definition 18.1, pp. 118–119, and Remark 29.7, p. 166

proof.text: Write $C_0=\operatorname{Spec}B$; then $C=\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_{k_0}k)$ by the affine fibre-product construction, so $C$ is affine. By [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change], $C$ is separated and of finite type over $k$. By [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence](1), its structure map is smooth of relative dimension one. Geometric connectedness in the statement gives that $C$ is nonempty and connected. Thus [lem-sbc-smooth-fixed-dimension-over-field] gives $\dim C=1$. These verify all the smooth connected curve hypotheses used below.

source.place: Tags 01T4 (lemma-base-change-finite-type), 01VB (lemma-base-change-smooth), 02NK (lemma-base-change-relative-dimension-d); separation: schemes.tex, Tag 01KU; dimension comparison: the cited smooth fixed-dimension node

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings](1) to $C$: it is Noetherian and integral. By [def-pc-integral-scheme], it is reduced and irreducible. The projection $p:C\to C_0$ is open by [lem-sc-scheme-over-field-universally-open], applied to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ over $k_0$. For any nonempty open $V\subset C$, the nonempty open $p(V)$ meets the dense open $U_0$; hence $V$ meets $p^{-1}(U_0)=U$. Thus $U$ is a nonempty dense open of $C$. It is irreducible, hence connected: two nonempty relatively open subsets of $U$ are nonempty opens of $C$ and intersect, since otherwise their closed complements would cover the irreducible space $C$ [def-weil-irreducible-components].

source.place: Tag 033M (lemma-normal-Noetherian), as specialized in the smooth connected curve node; integral: Tag 01ON (lemma-characterize-integral); openness: morphisms.tex, Tag 0383 (lemma-scheme-over-field-universally-open); irreducibility: topology.tex, Tag 004V

proof.text: Check the remaining hypotheses for the lisse fibre equivalence on $U$. Since $C$ is Noetherian, it is locally Noetherian; [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth] makes its affine coordinate ring $B\otimes_{k_0}k$ Noetherian. Hence $|C|$ is Noetherian by [lem-sc-affine-noetherian-underlying-space], and [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets] makes $U$ quasi-compact. It is locally Noetherian by the open-subscheme assertion in [pqf-def-locnoeth], so is Noetherian. It is separated over $k$: its diagonal is the restriction of the closed diagonal of $C$ to $U\times_k U$, with the restricted ideal sheaf defining that closed subscheme. Finally $\ell$ is invertible on $U$, since $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$.

source.place: Tags 01OV (definition-noetherian), 01OW (lemma-locally-Noetherian), 01OZ (lemma-Noetherian-topology); Noetherian subspaces: topology.tex, Tags 0052 (lemma-Noetherian), 04ZA (lemma-Noetherian-quasi-compact); open inheritance is stated in pqf-def-locnoeth

proof.text: If $C$ were proper over $k$, [lem-sc-proper-affine-finite] would make this affine curve finite over $k$, and in particular of dimension zero. This contradicts $\dim C=1$. Thus $C$ is not proper. Because $C$ is reduced, a closed subset $Z=|C|$ has reduced induced closed subscheme exactly $C$. By [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base](1), no closed subset proper over $k$ can therefore equal $|C|$.

source.place: Remark 29.7, p. 166, nonproperness in the support argument; proper closed subset convention: Stacks coherent.tex, Tags 0CYM/0CYL, and schemes.tex, Tag 01J4

proof.text: Put $G=j_*\mathcal F$ in degree zero. It is constructible by [lem-a1-adic-middle-extension-constructible]. For arbitrary $c\in H_c^0(C,G)$, apply [lem-a1-constructible-degree-zero-proper-support] to the separated finite-type geometric scheme $C$ and to $G$, in precisely the completed, rationalized, common-finite-stage coefficient category of the statement. It gives an injective section comparison $\alpha_{C,G}$ and a closed subset $Z\subset C$ proper over $k$, such that $s=\alpha_{C,G}(c)$ restricts to zero on $C\setminus Z$. Its open-restriction compatibility identifies $s|_U$ with an ordinary lisse adic section $t:\mathbf 1_U\to\mathcal F$. Here $G|_U=\mathcal F$: on a test object $V$ over $U$, the ordinary direct-image formula of [def-wf-middle-extension] reads $(j_*\mathcal F)(V)=\mathcal F(V\times_C U)=\mathcal F(V)$.

source.place: Definition 18.1 and Proposition 18.3(b), pp. 118–121; the cited constructible-section comparison explicitly supplies the adic extension and compatibility with lisse realization; Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15

proof.text: By step 4, $Z\ne C$, so $C\setminus Z$ is a nonempty open. Density of $U$ gives a point $u\in U\setminus Z$; choose a geometric point $\bar u$ above it. Since $s$ is zero on $C\setminus Z$, its restriction $t$ has zero fibre at $\bar u$. Apply clause (2) of [cor-galois-lisse-representations] on $U$: it is connected, Noetherian and separated by steps 2–3, and $\ell$ is invertible there. The geometric fibre functor on the stated finite-extension lisse $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-sheaves is an equivalence, hence faithful, and carries the coefficient unit to the trivial line. It therefore sends $t$ and the zero morphism to the same map only if $t=0$. This uses no assumption about purity, weights, or ramification.

source.place: Lemma 7.4.7, Remark 7.4.8 and Lemma 7.4.10; the finite-extension adic fibre equivalence is the statement of the cited Galois node

proof.text: For the ordinary direct image, a global section is determined by its restriction to $U$. Indeed, at a fixed coefficient sheaf stage a module morphism $s:\mathbf 1_C\to j_*\mathcal F$ is determined by the image of $1$; the formula $(j_*\mathcal F)(C)=\mathcal F(U)$ identifies this image with the section $t$, and all its components on test objects $V\to C$ are its pullbacks to $V\times_C U$ [def-wf-middle-extension]. Thus $t=0$ gives $s=0$. The same determination holds for an adic inverse system level by level; rationalization preserves this injective identification of Hom modules, and passing to a common finite extension and to idempotent summands preserves it by restriction to the corresponding Hom subspaces. Hence it applies to exactly the ordinary sheaf direct image used here. Since $\alpha_{C,G}$ is injective, $s=0$ implies $c=0$. As $c$ was arbitrary, $H_c^0(C,j_*\mathcal F)=0$.
